According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple was reportedly once considering a feature for its "Apple Upgrade" program that would make setting up an iPhone nearly seamless: having Apple pre-copy a user's data onto the new device. However, the feature never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: if users are regularly upgrading through fixed monthly installments, why not make the switch to a new phone as easy as possible? *Bloomberg* reporter Mark Gurman reports:

There are some obvious gaps here. First, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since the data transfer could only happen at the time of shipment—which lags a few days from the order date—unless you pick up in-store.

There's also the obvious privacy concern. That said, if you've been backing up to iCloud all along, Apple having your data shouldn't come as a surprise. But the average person might worry about how the data gets to the new phone, and whether anyone handles it in the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out an entirely new system in its retail stores called "Presto," which lets staff update an iPhone's system while it's still in the box. It's easy to imagine that system expanding in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, all without anyone touching your data.

Still, the feature never launched, and that may be a good thing.
